Transform your passion into purpose and elevate your career by taking the next step toward a graduate degree at RIT.
Start an Application
RIT Application
The following programs do not use RIT’s standard graduate application. Please apply directly through their specialized application system: Architecture M.Arch Online, Business Administration for Executives MBA, Dietetics and Nutrition MS, and Occupational Therapy OTD.
Not sure which path is right for you? Explore our full list of graduate degree programs to find your best fit.
Looking to apply for a doctoral program? Learn more
Manage Your Application
Log into Your Admissions Account
With an RIT admissions account, you can monitor your application, submit additional application materials, receive your admissions decision, see your next steps, and more.
If you need to change your submitted application, do not submit a new application. Please email gradinfo@rit.edu with your request (e.g. change academic program choices, change your term, withdraw application, etc).
Deadlines and Requirements
Application deadlines vary by degree and start term—though some programs accept applications year-round, we strongly encourage applying as early as possible.
Review Your Program's Deadlines and Requirements
What You Need to Apply
Application Materials
Online Application
The RIT online graduate application includes sections that will ask you to provide us with personal/biographical information, contact information, citizenship details, your past or current college/university and major/degree details, and test score data (if required by your degree), in addition to other profile data. If letter(s) of recommendation are required for your degree, you will be able to enter the names and contact information for each recommender. You will also be able to upload any supporting materials to your application. You may upload supporting documents while completing your online application or after you have submitted your application in your admissions portal. RIT prefers all supporting documents be submitted electronically.
1st Choice Program
While completing your application, you will need to select the 1st choice program (i.e. major, degree) you want to apply to.
2nd Choice Program
At RIT, you can submit one application and indicate up to 2 program choices. We encourage you to indicate a 2nd choice program. If you are not accepted to your 1st choice program, we will automatically facilitate a review for your 2nd choice. We will contact you if additional materials are required for your 2nd choice program.
Start Your Application
These applications are handled separately: Architecture M.Arch Online, Business Administration for Executives MBA, Dietetics and Nutrition MS, and Occupational Therapy OTD.
Application Fee
To be considered for graduate study, you are required to pay a non-refundable $65 application fee. Your application fee can be paid within your admissions portal after you submit your application.
Current RIT students and RIT alumni are not required to pay the $65.00 application fee. The application fee will be waived within 24 hours of the submission of your application.
Transcript(s)
RIT requires transcripts from all colleges and universities that you have attended, including transcript grading keys.
International students should provide transcripts (or mark sheets) and degree certificates from all post-secondary institutions.
To submit your transcript(s) for application review:
Upload copies or official transcript(s) with the submission of your online application, or
Upload your transcript(s) through your admissions portal after you have submitted your application
Upon enrollment at RIT, you will need to contact your prior college or university and request that your official, final records be sent directly to RIT. Documents you upload are not considered official. To learn more about sending official transcripts upon enrollment, select your applicable accepted student checklist and navigate to the transcripts section.
RIT does not require a WES evaluation or other academic credential review. If we are unable to determine your bachelor’s degree equivalency or need further information our admissions office will contact you.
Degree Requirements
All applicants to RIT’s graduate programs must hold—or currently be completing—a four-year baccalaureate degree, or the equivalent of a U.S. bachelor’s degree, granted by an accredited college or university.
If you have not yet completed your undergraduate coursework, your admission will be contingent upon submission of your final transcript showing the degree granted and the date of the degree.
3-Year Degrees from International Universities
RIT will review applicants with 3-year degrees from international universities. Students with 3-year degrees from India must meet all of the following conditions:
The college or university is WHED recognized, and
The college or university is NAAC accredited with an "A" grade, and
You have passed in the 1st Class (or equivalent).
If you do not meet the above requirements, you may request a WES evaluation or you would need to complete (or be in the process of) postgraduate study.
If your 3-year undergraduate degree is currently in progress, you may be admitted contingent upon obtaining your degree in the 1st class or equivalent.
Higher National Diplomas (HNDs) from Nigeria or Ghana
RIT considers Higher National Diplomas (HNDs) from Nigeria or Ghana to be comparable to U.S. bachelor’s degrees under the following conditions: the HND is a 2-year program that followed a 2-year National Diploma (ND) or Ordinary National Diploma (OND) program, for a total of at least 4 years of post-secondary study.
Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Upload a resume or curriculum vitae (CV) to your online application. Your resume or curriculum vitae (CV) should include details about your education, employment, and internship history. Pertinent research experience should be included as well.
Personal Statement of Educational Objectives
Please upload a personal statement describing your educational objectives. The goal of the personal statement is to introduce yourself to the Admissions Committee. There is no minimum or maximum page length or word count.
The format is open-ended, but you may wish to address:
Why you are applying for the program, such as your goals and your passion as it relates to the program of interest
How your degree program will relate to your long-range career objectives
What personal or “non-academic” qualities you will contribute to the learning environment in your program
What prior academic or research experience you have with respect to your chosen program
Specifically why you want to attend RIT
Statement of Purpose for Research Doctoral programs only
Students applying to a doctoral program must upload a statement of purpose for research to your online application that will allow the Admissions Committee to learn the most about you as a prospective researcher.
Each program has specific guidelines for the statement of purpose for research. Find your program's guidelines
Letters of Recommendation varies by program
One or more letters of recommendation are required for admission to all RIT graduate programs except those offered by the College of Business. Recommendations should come from members of the academic community and/or workplace professionals who know your qualifications for graduate study.
Submit Letter(s) of Recommendation
Within the online application, you are able to enter information for your recommenders and submit an email request for letters. Recommendation letters should be submitted directly to RIT from the referee/person writing the letter for you.
The preferred method for the submission of recommendation letters is to use the functionality within the online application. If your recommenders are unable to submit their letters using the above method, then letters may be emailed directly by recommenders to gradinfo@rit.edu or sent by postal mail to the Graduate Admissions office.
Test Scores (GRE/GMAT) varies by program
Test Score Requirements
Only some degrees require a GMAT (Graduate Management Admissions Test) or GRE (Graduate Record Examination).
Find a degree's test requirements
Submit Test Results
You may self-report test scores on your application. Your uploaded test score copy will be considered unofficial. The unofficial copy will update your checklist when both the copy and the hand-entered scores are entered on the Test Scores page in your application or in the portal.‍
Submission of official scores may be a contingency of your admission. If you are required to submit official score reports, you must arrange for the testing agency to send your test results directly to RIT’s Graduate Admissions office.
RIT's code for ETS reporting is 2760. You may choose any department code. All test scores will be sent to Graduate Admissions in a test score file within 10-14 days regardless of the department code selected.
Ensure that the email address used for your application matches the email used with your testing agency.
Troubleshooting
Q: I sent my test scores. Why has my application checklist not been updated?
A: If the email address or name used on your application is different than the email address or name on your score report, your test score checklist may not update to “received.” Please email gradinfo@rit.edu with this concern and note the name difference.
Writing Sample and/or Essay varies by program
Most programs have the option to submit a writing sample as part of your application.
The following programs require a writing sample:
Criminal Justice MS
Cognitive Science Ph.D.
Instructions: Your writing sample may be an example of your research, publications, project, or other scholarly written work.
Sustainable Systems MS
Sustainability Ph.D.
Instructions: Submit a writing sample, of your own work, in which you are the only author. This can be a report or paper from previous academic or professional work that reflects your critical thinking and writing abilities. Published papers listing your name as one of several authors in a group will not be accepted and do not meet the application requirements.
Portfolio varies by program
View the admissions requirements section on your degree page to determine if a portfolio is required by the program to which you seek admission. Find your degree's page
If a portfolio is required, locate your degree on the portfolio requirements page and follow the guidelines for submitting your portfolio.
English Language Test Scores varies by applicant
English Language Test Requirements
Self-reported test scores for Duolingo (DET), IELTS, LanguageCert Academic, PTE Academic, and TOEFL are accepted to apply. Scores can be reported in the Test Score section of the application or in your admissions portal after you have submitted your application.
Your uploaded test score copy will be considered unofficial. The unofficial copy will update your checklist when both the copy and the hand-entered scores are entered on the Test Scores page in your application or in the portal.‍ If admitted, official English score reports will be required prior to your first term of enrollment, as a contingency of your admission.
English Language Test Scores are required of all international applicants who do not meet the requirements outlined in the waiver section below.
View the overall minimum score requirement for your intended program in the graduate admission deadlines and requirements table.
In addition, each program requires balanced sub-scores when determining an applicant’s need for additional English language courses. For example, a minimum overall score of 88, will require sub-scores of 22 for Reading, Writing, Speaking, and Listening.
Deaf and hard-of-hearing test takers with significant hearing loss do not need to take the listening and speaking sections for the TOEFL and IELTS. Scores from these sections will not be considered in the review of application materials because the listening/speaking components of the TOEFL and IELTS sections are not relevant for deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals.
Exams Accepted
Duolingo English Test
IELTS Academic and IELTS Academic Online
LanguageCert Academic
PTE Academic
TOEFL iBT® and TOEFL iBT® Home Edition (except for MyBest Score)1
Exams NOT Accepted
TOEFL Essentials
IELTS General
TOEFL MyBest Scores
Letters from your college or university indicating "English proficiency" or letters indicating courses were taught in English in place of official English language test scores.
1 As of January 21, 2026, the TOEFL iBT® test transitioned to a new 1–6 band scoring scale. Because TOEFL scores are valid for two years, we are listing both the old (0–120) and new (1–6) scales in the graduate admission deadlines and requirements table to accommodate applicants who took the test before or after this change. We accept official scores from either version of the test, provided they are within the two-year validity period.
Submitting Official Test Scores
You must arrange for the testing agency to send your test results directly to RIT’s Graduate Admissions office. Only official exam results received this way will be considered. Uploaded copies of your test score reports will not update your checklist item to “received.”
RIT's code for ETS (TOEFL) reporting is 2760. You may choose any department code. All test scores will be sent to Graduate Admissions in a test score file within 10-14 days regardless of the department code selected. Allow an additional 3 - 5 days from the date RIT should receive the official scores for processing and checklist updates.
IELTS score reports may be sent to us electronically or in paper format from the testing agency. If you have concerns about your IELTS score report, please email gradinfo@rit.edu.
Ensure that the email address used for your application matches the email used with your testing agency.
Troubleshooting
Q: I requested my official test scores to be sent to RIT through the testing agency. Why has my application checklist not been updated?
A: If the email address or name used on your application is different than the email address or name on your score report, your test score checklist may not update to “received.” Please email gradinfo@rit.edu with this concern.
English Test Requirement Waivers
International Applicants may be considered for a waiver of an english language proficiency exam if:
They have worked or studied in the U.S. for the last two years, and/or
They have completed bachelor’s or master’s degree from an English-medium university from the territories on the list below, and/or
They are citizens of the territories below and have completed secondary school at an English-medium school.
RIT has determined those countries/territories to be the following:
American Samoa
Australia
Bahamas
Barbados
Belize
Bermuda
Canada
Commonwealth Caribbean
England
Guam
Ireland
Kenya
Mauritius
New Zealand
Scotland
Singapore
South Africa
Virgin Islands
Wales
Audiogram deaf or hard-of-hearing students only
Deaf or hard-of-hearing students must submit an unaided audiogram to be considered for the reduced tuition rate.
Your admissions portal provides a checklist to help determine any additional materials you need to complete your application. Your application will be sent for review to the Admissions Committee once all required items have been submitted.
Applying for Doctoral Programs
Are you applying for doctoral study?
Applying for a doctoral program requires more diligence and patience than applying for a Master’s degree. To stand out from a competitive pool of candidates, you must prepare a strong application that includes your academic achievements, any related research experience, and a clear statement of your research interests and goals. Our team has prepared a resource to help you navigate the application process for doctoral programs.
Learn How to Apply for a Doctoral Program
After You Apply
Once the application is received, your graduate admissions counselor will contact you via email to acknowledge receipt of your application—and tell you if any necessary items are missing from your application.
You may log in to your admissions portal at any time to monitor and track the receipt of your application credentials, upload new supporting documents, change your email address or password and follow us on social media! Your admissions portal also hosts a checklist to aid in determining what is needed to complete your application. Log into your admissions portal
How to Make Edits After Submitting
If you need changes or updates made to your application after submission, email gradinfo@rit.edu. Please do not submit a second application.
If you did not indicate a 2nd choice program on your application, you may contact us to add one.
Review Process and Timeline
The Graduate Admissions office and each college's department work closely and carefully to review each application submitted.
Once the application is received by your graduate enrollment counselor. Your counselor will contact you if any necessary items are missing from your application.
When your application has been sent to the admissions committee for review. Each graduate department makes its own admission decisions on its own schedule. Typically, the decision process takes 2-3 weeks. In some cases, especially for PhD admission, the review process may take up to 12 weeks or more.
Some programs will not start the review process until after the priority deadline and if this is the case, you will see a “hold for program review deadline” administrative checklist item in your admissions portal. This checklist item keeps your application with the Graduate Admissions office until the priority deadline date. All complete applications will be sent to the admissions committee for review after the priority deadline.
Once a decision has been made on your admissions status you will be notified by email to check the update in your admissions portal. Here you can view your official decision and related information.
Check Your Application Status
You can log into your admissions portal at any time to monitor your application progress, track the status of your application credentials, receive your admissions decision, view next steps, register for events and view recorded information sessions, and more.
Obtaining an International Student Visa
Our team is here to help you understand the next steps for applying for your student visa. To apply for a student visa, U.S. government regulations require international students to demonstrate that they have sufficient financial resources to meet the costs of tuition, fees, supplies, and living expenses for at least nine months of full-time study.
Learn next steps for obtaining or maintaining your student visa
